mechanism_rules.mechanism: biallelic reduced BUBR1 abundance or specific checkpoint/attachment dysfunction
mechanism_rules.notes: Functional studies show distinct effects on BUBR1 abundance and checkpoint or attachment function. A predicted truncation or missense change does not establish the residual activity of either allele, and two apparent null alleles are not assumed equivalent to studied genotypes.

mechanism_rules.mechanism: biallelic CEP57 loss affecting centrosome and microtubule function
mechanism_rules.notes: Biallelic loss-of-function alleles were established in the original study. The model recognizes a compatible consequence class only; exon relevance, RNA effect and technical validity still require review.

mechanism_rules.mechanism: biallelic TRIP13 deficiency impairing spindle checkpoint regulation
mechanism_rules.notes: Patient-cell experiments demonstrated TRIP13 deficiency and chromosome missegregation. This rule applies to the specified MVA-associated disease, not every reproductive disorder associated with TRIP13.

mechanism_rules.mechanism: biallelic CENATAC dysfunction altering minor-intron splicing
mechanism_rules.notes: Reported mutant transcripts encode altered C-terminal proteins. A coding missense annotation can conceal a splice effect; arbitrary truncations are not presumed identical to the studied alleles.

mechanism_rules.mechanism: biallelic loss of full-length MAD1 with spindle checkpoint deficiency
mechanism_rules.notes: A primary human study linked biallelic variants to absent full-length protein and checkpoint dysfunction. Other MAD1L1 disease associations do not inherit this mechanism automatically.

mechanism_rules.mechanism: biallelic reduction of BUB1 abundance or kinase activity
mechanism_rules.notes: The reported individuals retained different amounts of protein or kinase activity. Their chromosome-segregation disorder resembles aspects of MVA but is not interchangeable with every MVA syndrome.

mechanism_rules.mechanism: biallelic truncation impairing p31comet stability and checkpoint silencing
mechanism_rules.notes: The source reports biallelic truncating alleles with instability and interaction defects. This explicitly sourced literature profile is separate from other gene-disease identifiers; no OMIM equivalence is invented.

mechanism_rules.mechanism: biallelic CEP192 dysfunction associated with spindle and centrosome defects
mechanism_rules.notes: The source studied particular biallelic missense alleles and distinguished monoallelic infertility associations. Generic truncation is not automatically treated as an equivalent MVA mechanism.

mechanism_rules.mechanism: biallelic hypomorphic SLF2 dysfunction in DNA replication and genome maintenance
mechanism_rules.notes: The reported disorder includes replication stress, segmented chromosomes and large chromosome gains. Transcript-dependent splicing effects and residual function require review.

mechanism_rules.mechanism: biallelic hypomorphic SMC5 dysfunction in DNA replication and chromosome maintenance
mechanism_rules.notes: Missense, in-frame and truncating alleles were studied in a hypomorphic disease context. Consequence severity alone does not establish a compatible pair.

mechanism_rules.mechanism: specific altered CDC20 checkpoint interactions rather than generic haploinsufficiency
mechanism_rules.notes: The study distinguished the effect of a particular heterozygous missense allele from heterozygous knockout. No arbitrary CDC20 truncation is promoted by this rule, and the reported de novo status is not transferred to the analyzed individual.

scoring_interpretation: Uncalibrated review utility; no confidence or probability is generated. Unknown phase is a review requirement, not a probability multiplier.
